doc_friction.issue: Drew hearth-and-horizon, whose only waiting proposal was already being written in open PR #16355; the draw cannot see open PRs, so the run had to search and fall back by hand.

The For Other Minds proposal specified a 'six-week reading log' as the second look; in the story's timeline (letters 2 Oct, half-term, second look to 11 Dec) a fixed six weeks did not fit, so the story uses the term-long reading record instead.

Searched open PRs before drafting and found none on the screener proposal, but another session (PR #16360) opened and merged it while this run drafted; a bible proposal has no claim marker, so two sessions can pick the same 'next up' entry within an hour. A claim line in BIBLE.md (or a draft PR opened before drafting) would prevent it.

deviations.why: Its 'then:' fallback listed saints-by-candlelight first, but For Other Minds had the highest draw weight (35%) and a fully specified bible proposal, while Saints had just landed episode 125 an hour earlier.
deviations.did: Wrote the For Other Minds proposal instead of a Saints episode.
deviations.result: Story landed with numbers checked; no open PR overlapped.

deviations.why: After the merge conflict showed #16360 had landed the same proposal, merging a second story on the same premise would have duplicated the shelf.
deviations.did: Dropped 'Nine Letters Home' before merging and wrote 'Ninety-Seven Visits' (Goodhart's law) from the For Other Minds proposal this run had added to the bible.
deviations.result: Second story landed; the first draft cost about a story's worth of tokens and is not in the tree.

notes: Project: Hearth & Horizon, For Other Minds shelf. Piece: ninety-seven-visits (Goodhart's law: visits target, then minutes target, then four figures plus notes). A first draft, nine-letters-home (reading screener), was dropped unmerged because PR #16360 merged the same bible proposal meanwhile. Text only (audio 474 MB > 400 MB cap). node --test 17/17; run_workflow_locally --for-changes 12/12 on the first draft's diff.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a writer drafting and fact-checking a 2,900-word statistics short story plus a blog post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
